title: Recognising Ground Under Repair
question: Which area is most likely to be marked as 'ground under repair' where you may get relief?

choices.text: A blue-marked area with piles of grass cuttings
A patch of bare earth not marked by anything
A normal bunker filled with sand
A spot of wet grass after rain

explanation: Ground under repair is usually marked with lines or stakes (commonly blue or white) and can include areas with piled grass from maintenance.

juniorVersion.title: Spotting Ground Under Repair
juniorVersion.question: Which place is usually marked as 'ground under repair' so you can take relief?

choices.text: A blue-marked area with piles of grass clippings
A patch of bare dirt with nothing on it
A regular bunker full of sand
Some wet grass after it rains

juniorVersion.explanation: Ground under repair is often shown with blue lines or sticks. It can be a spot with lots of cut grass left by the greenkeeper.

vocabulary.simpleMeaning: A part of the course marked with lines or stakes because it is being fixed. You may be allowed to move your ball from here.
A free chance to move your ball without penalty when there is something wrong with the ground.
Pieces of grass that have been cut and left in a pile.

juniorVersion.teachingTip: Show children what ground under repair markers look like and explain why these spots are fixed or unsafe.
likelyMisconceptions: Children might think any bare patch of earth or any wet spot is 'ground under repair'. Remind them to look for lines or markers.
Children might confuse grass clippings with normal grass or not notice markers.
